messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (us-west-2) — paging sre-oncall. Automated mitigation: routing fallback to us-east started. Please acknowledge.

Taylor (oncall): Acked, looking. I can see error spike in gen-queue and a few OOMs on node-gpu-12.

Amanda: Thanks. Can we get an initial customer-facing blurb ready? I'll shepherd publish once we have legal ok.

Taylor (oncall): Working on mitigation — draining node-gpu-12, shifting traffic to warm pool, increasing batch timeout to lower memory pressure. ETA 6–8 min.

Amanda: Draft for initial notice (copy suggestion):
```
We are investigating increased error rates and latency for text generation in the US-West region. Some requests are returning 5xx or timing out. Engineers are actively investigating and traffic is being routed to a fallback region to reduce customer impact. We will post updates within 15 minutes or sooner.
Impact: Partial degradation of generation endpoints in US-West only.
What we're doing: Rerouting traffic, draining affected worker, increasing resilience timeouts.
```

Ryan: +1 to that copy. Maybe add: "No data exposure suspected at this time."

Sophie: LegalBot, can you quick-check the wording? Avoid implying root cause.

LegalBot: Quick note: remove phrase "infrastructure fault" and avoid commitment of specific ETA. Suggest: replace "Engineers are actively investigating" with "Teams are investigating." Also approve adding "No customer data is believed to be exposed."

Amanda: Edited draft below per legal: 
```
We are investigating increased error rates and latency for text generation in the US-West region. Some requests are returning 5xx or timing out. Teams are investigating and traffic is being routed to a fallback region to reduce customer impact. We will post updates as we learn more.
Impact: Partial degradation of generation endpoints in US-West only.
What we're doing: Rerouting traffic, draining affected worker, increasing resilience timeouts.
No customer data is believed to be exposed.
```

Taylor (oncall): Mitigation progress: drained node-gpu-12, memory pressure reduced on warm pool. Error rate down ~60%. Hold publishing initial notice for 2 mins while we confirm stability.

Amanda: Understood. Ping me when you want me to publish.

Taylor (oncall): Confirm stable for last 90s, error rate trending down. You have clearance to publish initial notice.

Amanda: Publishing initial notice now. Posting to status page and sending templated customer email to impacted customers.

Amanda: (posted) "Initial update" published to status page. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/4850001234 — please check for typos.

Sophie: Quick copy edit request for status page line 2: change "timing out" -> "experiencing timeouts". Amanda can you patch?

Amanda: Patched.

Taylor (oncall): Follow-up update at +15m: error rate stable at baseline, still monitoring. No escalation required. Recommend scheduling resolved notice once we hit 30m stable.

Amanda: Drafting follow-up update for status page and customer note: 
```
Update: Error rates have decreased and service is returning to normal for most customers. Traffic remains routed away from the affected worker while we complete post-incident cleanup. We will continue to monitor and provide a final update when fully resolved.
```

LegalBot: Approved. No further edits.

Ryan: Thx. Suggest adding brief postmortem action: look into batch timeout defaults and autoscale thresholds.

Taylor (oncall): Agreed — adding jira task after incident.

(30 minutes later)

Taylor (oncall): Service appears fully recovered for 35 minutes, error rate back to normal across regions. No residual OOMs.

Amanda: Drafting resolved notice: 
```
Resolved: The elevated error rates and latency affecting text generation in US-West have been resolved. Root cause: transient memory pressure on a worker node causing OOMs; traffic was rerouted and affected workers were drained. Mitigations included routing fallback, draining the worker, and increasing resilience timeouts.
Impact: Customers may have experienced increased errors during the incident window; no customer data is believed to have been exposed.
Next steps: A post-incident investigation will be opened to review autoscale and batching defaults.
```

LegalBot: Small wording change: replace "Root cause:" with "Primary contributing factor:" (avoid definitive language until postmortem).

Amanda: Updated resolved copy and publishing now.

Amanda: (posted) Resolved notice published to status page and customer emails queued. Closing thread from comms side.

Taylor (oncall): Closing oncall-side. Will file postmortem draft and ping ops for RCA.

Amanda: Thanks all — great quick coordination. :thumbsup:
